context.handler: one hard-IRQ-like hdq_isr invocation reached after registration ordering
context.lifetime: the fixture object is static; real devm lifetime and remove-time IRQ teardown are source-reviewed but not analyzed
context.memory_order: Mthread interleavings and locksets only; no LKMM or ARM weak-memory claim
context.preemption: configured non-RT spin_lock_irqsave disables preemption in source; task/task scheduling is outside the selected process/hard-IRQ property
context.process: one process-context hdq_reset_irqstatus invocation reached after lock initialization
context.remote_cpu: local IRQ masking is CPU-local and only hdq-spinlock is shared
context.same_cpu: the process mask interval and whole handler share cpu0-local-irq

entry_adapter.argument: Probe initializes hdq_spinlock before devm_request_irq. The adapter likewise initializes both abstract locks before creating one independently analyzed handler entry. One reached invocation is sufficient only for the site-based access-protection property; recurrence, nesting, priorities and liveness are excluded. Frama-C 33 automatic handlers instead start from main's initial state and cannot consume this probe-time initialization.

limitations: No automatic-handler initialization, repeated delivery, nesting, priorities, FIQ/NMI, softirq, threaded IRQ, affinity migration or CPU-hotplug semantics are accepted.
interrupts.scope: One abstract post-probe hard-IRQ entry, separately checked for same-CPU local masking and remote-CPU spinlock exclusion.

limitations: No whole-object race freedom, functional status protocol, wait-queue ordering, weak-memory ordering or lock implementation proof follows.
mutex_protected_concurrency.scope: Only Mthread lockset classification of the selected irqstatus accesses in the two token-identical OMAP HDQ functions.

limitations: The same-CPU functional no-overlap assertion remains Unknown and is a recorded precision boundary, not an accepted assertion.
sequential.scope: Only the named adapter-result assertions in this exact fixture.

linux_hdq_spinlock.conservative_argument: For access protection only, the configured non-RT SMP spinlock admits one owner across CPUs. Both copied critical sections route through the same abstract lock, and a remote-CPU lock-elided control must remove that common lockset.
limitations: The atomic spin algorithm, contention, fairness, deadlock, acquire/release ordering and PREEMPT_RT behavior are not modeled.
linux_hdq_spinlock.semantics: One successful Mthread mutex acquisition/release represents exclusive ownership of hdq_spinlock around the copied source critical sections.

linux_local_irq_mask.conservative_argument: The configured ARM local IRQ save disables IRQ entry on that CPU; the handler entry and selected process interval share the gate. A mask-elided control must expose the model marker while leaving the data spinlock active.
limitations: Only CPU0 and ordinary hard IRQs are represented; nested masking depth, FIQ/NMI, softirq, migration and exact entry/return state are excluded.
linux_local_irq_mask.semantics: One per-CPU abstract mutex represents exclusion between the process critical interval after local_irq_save and the entire same-CPU hard-IRQ invocation.

post_init_hardirq_entry.conservative_argument: For a site-based lockset property, the independent handler entry exposes the selected process/handler access pairs and arbitrary cross-entry interference after the source-supported initialization point. No completion fact is consumed.
limitations: The adapter is not Linux IRQ registration or delivery and does not model recurrence, nesting, priority or liveness.
post_init_hardirq_entry.semantics: A pthread-created Mthread entry invokes the exact handler body once after both model locks are initialized.

property.claim: For the one post-initialization process/handler pair, every selected irqstatus access inside the token-identical hdq_reset_irqstatus critical section and hdq_isr locked update carries hdq-spinlock; same-CPU entry is additionally classified under the local IRQ gate and remote-CPU exclusion relies on the shared spinlock.
exclusions: The unlocked hdq_isr status read remains visible and is not accepted as protected on a remote CPU.
Whole-variable or whole-driver data-race freedom is not claimed; unlocked wait predicates and logging are outside this property.
No functional status protocol, wakeup correctness, MMIO behavior, handler recurrence, nesting or priority property is checked.
Softirq, threaded IRQ, FIQ/NMI, PREEMPT_RT, affinity migration, CPU hotplug, teardown lifetime and nested locks are not supported.
No weak-memory, compiler ordering, atomic, RCU, lock-free, deadlock, fairness, progress or termination property is checked.

remaining_concurrency: C3 weak-memory, atomics and lock-free reasoning
C4 RCU lifetime and combined concurrency coverage
Broader IRQ classes, recurrence, nesting, priorities and teardown
The preserved unlocked HDQ status accesses require separate review
